_meta.project: JOCKY — a domain-specific language for computer and network forensic analysis
_meta.platform_note: All timings are wall-clock on a single laptop, mean of repeated runs. They are throughput ratios for comparison, not absolute speed claims. Report them as such.
_meta.honesty_note: Every number here was produced by code in the repository and can be regenerated with `python deck/bench.py && python deck/bench_baseline.py`. Nothing is estimated or invented. The unfavourable numbers (interpreter overhead) are included deliberately and should appear in the paper.

units.records_per_sec: records processed per second during execution
units.overhead_x: jocky_ms / python_ms — how many times slower than the equivalent hand-written Python

table_scaling.caption: Table 1 — Interpreter scaling across synthetic evidence volumes. Cost is linear in record count and lex/parse cost is independent of it.

table_overhead_vs_python.caption: Table 2 — Interpreter overhead against a hand-written Python implementation of the same investigation, plus isolated evidence-load time.

table_result_stability.caption: Table 3 — Result stability. The same investigation over the same evidence yields identical findings, record counts and evidence digests at every scale. Only the wall-clock duration varies between runs.
table_result_stability.note: Two consecutive --json runs of the same script differ in exactly one field, duration_ms. Everything else, including findings, records and digests, is byte-identical.

table_evidence_corpus.caption: Table 4 — The synthetic evidence corpus for case SIH-2026-014 on host FIN-WS-014.

table_lex_parse.caption: Table 5 — Compiler front-end cost, which is independent of evidence volume.
table_lex_parse.note: A 332-token, 101-node script parses in 2.2-3.1 ms across all four evidence scales, so front-end cost is independent of data volume. This is what makes a script reviewable before it touches evidence.

table_codebase.caption: Table 6 — Implementation size, in lines. No third-party dependencies; Python 3.11+ standard library only.

figure_1_execution_time.caption: Figure 1 — Execution time against record count. Linear, slope ~0.177 ms/record.

figure_2_throughput.caption: Figure 2 — Throughput stays flat across three orders of magnitude, i.e. the interpreter has no superlinear behaviour at these scales.

figure_3_memory.caption: Figure 3 — Peak interpreter memory against record count. Linear, ~1.25 KB per record.

figure_4_overhead.caption: Figure 4 — Interpreter overhead against hand-written Python. This is the paper's honest cost, not a defect to bury.

figure_5_parse_cost_flat.caption: Figure 5 — Lex and parse cost is flat across evidence volume, because it depends on script size, not data size.

peak_kb_per_record.note: Remarkably constant at ~1.25 KB per record.

provenance_rejection_demo.input: finding "Something I did not actually query" severity high from ghost_data
provenance_rejection_demo.point: The central design claim. A finding that does not name the result set that raised it is refused by the language, not merely discouraged by convention.

determinism_demo.method: Run the same script twice with --json and compare, excluding the wall-clock duration_ms field.
determinism_demo.point: Findings, record counts, evidence digests and timeline are reproducible. Only the run's own timing varies, which is a measurement of the machine rather than part of the case.
